paper.title: Competing Bandits in Matching Markets via Super Stability

unmapped: two-sided matching market: N users and K arms (N <= K) each with unknown preferences over the other side
objective is to reach a stable matching; regret measured as user/arm-pessimal stable regret and binary stable regret
true preferences have no ties (strict full rank)
settings.definition_quote: We consider the matching markets with two-sided uncertainty. There are $N$ users and $K$ arms... where $\eta_{i,j}(t)$ and $\eta'_{j,i}(t)$ are independent $1$-subgaussian noise... Centralized: In this setting, in each round the arms and users reveal their learned preferences to a central platform.

settings.name_in_paper: Decentralized two-sided matching bandit (2 shared flags)
unmapped: two-sided matching market with decentralized users proposing to arms; collisions give zero reward
users share two global binary flags (restart, success)
objective is a stable matching; pessimal stable / binary stable regret
settings.definition_quote: Decentralized: In this setting, in each round the users can propose to the arms (possibly multiple). Each arm can accept and match with at most one user... Additionally, users have access to 2 shared flags (binary semaphores).

settings.name_in_paper: Centralized two-sided matching bandit (lower bound, Bernoulli rewards)
unmapped: two-sided matching market; binary stable regret counts rounds where the played matching is not stable
settings.definition_quote: Our system is parameterized by $\theta = (\boldsymbol{\mu}, \boldsymbol{\gamma}) \in \Theta := [0,1]^{2 N K}$. We focus on Bernoulli rewards with appropriate means for ease of exposition.

algorithms.name: Centralized Two-Sided Matching Bandit (UCB-LCB partial ranks + Extended Gale-Shapley, round-robin exploration)

symbols.Delta_A: admissible gap: largest minimum gap over admissible partial ranks

source.label: thm:centralized_main
source.quote: The cumulative regret of Algorithm~\ref{alg:centralized} in $T$ rounds for the true stable matching instance with no ties ... \mathbb{E}[R_{0/1}(T)] \leq (K + \frac{NK \pi^2}{3} + \frac{96 K\log(T)}{\Delta^2_{\mathcal{A}}})

results.notes: Bound on expected binary stable regret; the theorem also states each user's/arm's pessimal stable regret normalized by (mu_pess - mu_min) is at most this quantity. Quantity mapped to 'other'.

conditions: users share two global binary flags

source.label: thm:decentralized_main
source.quote: For a true stable matching instance $(F^*_{u}, F^*_{a})$ when the users follow Algorithm~\ref{alg:decentralizedUser}, and the arms follow Algorithm~\ref{alg:decentralizedArm}, ... \mathbb{E}[R_{0/1}(T)] \leq (1 + N^2 + K + \frac{NK \pi^2}{3} + \frac{96 K\log(T)}{\Delta^2_{\mathcal{A}}})

results.notes: Binary stable regret bound; also bounds normalized pessimal stable regret of each user/arm.

symbols.c_theta: value of the Graves-Lai-type LP over matchings with bad set Lambda(theta) (instances sharing no stable matching with theta, unchanged on Locked edges)

source.label: thm:centralized_lower
source.quote: For any instance $\theta \in \Theta$, for any {\em uniformly good} policy $\pi$ the binary stable regret is lower bounded as $\lim\inf_{T\to \infty} \frac{\mathbb{E}[R_{0/1}^{\pi}(T; \theta)]}{\log(T)} \geq c(\theta)$, where $c(\theta)$ minimizes the following optimization problem ...

results.notes: Binary stable regret. Not using C_lin since the LP is specific (multiple optimal solutions). Theorem F.1 (adapted from Combes et al.) restates it.

symbols.c_SD: max over users i and arms j of c_{u,i} = sum_{j in D_i} 1/kl(gamma_{j,i},gamma_{j,j}) + sum_{j>i} 1/kl(mu_{i,j},mu_{i,i}) and c_{a,j} = sum_{i: j in D_i} 1/kl(gamma_{j,i},gamma_{j,j}) + sum_{i<j} 1/kl(mu_{i,j},mu_{i,i})

conditions: general serial dictatorship: all arms share preference i < i'

source.quote: Consider a general serial dictatorship instance $\theta$ with two sided uncertainty, where $N\leq K$, $\gamma_{j,i}(\theta) > \gamma_{j,i'}(\theta)$ for all $i < i'$ and $j$, and the unique stable matching is $\{(i,i): i \in [N]\}$. Then the binary stable regret ... is lower bounded as ...

symbols.c_RA: max of c_{u,i} = sum_{j unlocked} 1/kl(mu_{i,j}, mu_{i,j*(i)}) over users and c_{a,j} = sum_i 1/kl(mu_{i,j}, mu_{i,j*(i)}) over unlocked arms j

source.quote: Consider a general two-sided stable matching instance $\theta$ with redundant arms $N < K$, where $j^*(i) \triangleq \max_{j}\{ \mu_{i,j}(\theta): (i,j) \in Locked(\theta)\}$. Then the binary stable regret ... is lower bounded as ...

symbols.c_CG: max over non-connected cover groups G of sum_{C in G} 1/kl(theta, C)

source.label: thm:centralized_lower_final
source.quote: The value of $c(\theta)$ in Theorem~\ref{thm:centralized_lower_combes} is lower bounded by the value $c_{\varepsilon}(\theta)$ ... Furthermore, $c(\theta)$ satisfies the following lower bound $c(\theta) \geq \max_{G \in \mathcal{CG}(\theta)}\sum_{C\in G} kl(\theta, C)^{-1}$

results.notes: Combined with Theorem 5.1 gives liminf binary stable regret / log T >= this quantity. Also gives a dual LP lower bound c_eps(theta), not separately recorded.
